conflicts.fact: Which lesson quantifies atmospheric pressure and explains why our bodies are not crushed
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says Lesson 4 will quantify atmospheric pressure and explain why bodies are not crushed. Lesson 1 gives the body explanation early. Lesson 4 quantifies the pressure (101.3 kPa), but its Explain phase and summary do not cover bodies, only raising it as a DQB question.

conflicts.fact: When the jerrycan model was started and which model is being updated
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 starts a jerrycan force-arrow model. Lesson 8 says the cumulative model is a cross-sectional diagram of a liquid container updated since Lesson 1, and also says the model has been growing since Lesson 4.

conflicts.fact: Whether the jerrycan was full of water or empty/what was done to it, and recovery on reopening
conflicts.versions: The anchoring phenomenon describes opening a full jerrycan, pouring out water, resealing and removing air. Lesson 1 uses a sealed empty jerrycan and says that on reopening it partially recovered. Lesson 9 says it re-inflates by pumping air in and 'pops back to its original shape', and that the jerrycan from Lesson 1 is still crushed.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons in the sequence
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the questions will drive the next 19 lessons. Lesson 9 is the final unit synthesis lesson, and it refers to nine lessons.
Lesson 4 says ~101.3 kPa. Lesson 8 uses ~100,000 Pa. Lesson 9 uses 101,325 Pa, and a Nairobi value of 83,000 Pa.

conflicts.fact: Bottle size and hole heights in the jet experiment
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 uses a 1.5-litre bottle with holes at 5, 12 and 20 cm from the base. Lesson 6 uses a 2-litre bottle with holes at 5, 15 and 25 cm. Lesson 6 also presents it as a repeat of the Lesson 3 investigation.

conflicts.fact: Load mass used in the syringe hydraulic investigation
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 uses a 50 g mass. Lesson 7 says it rebuilds the Lesson 5 model with a heavier 200 g load; consistent in intent, but Lesson 7's tubing is 40 cm versus Lesson 5's 30 cm.
Lesson 9 requires students to use Boyle's Law (PV = constant) and a pressure differential equation, yet no earlier lesson in the sequence teaches Boyle's Law.

conflicts.fact: Whether liquid pressure acts outward/direction and the Pascal-principle explanation of jerrycan walls
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 says Pascal's principle explains why the force on the jerrycan is uniform across walls, while Lessons 5 and 7 say the jerrycan collapse is NOT Pascal's principle (uncontrolled pressure difference), contradicting Lesson 9.
